content.content:
1	# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform
2	
3	Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
8	- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
9	- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
10	- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
11	- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
12	- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).
13	
14	## Portals & design system
15	
16	**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.
17	
18	- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
19	  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
20	  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
21	  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).
22	
23	- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
24	  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
25	  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
26	  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).
27	
28	- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
29	  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
30	  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
31	  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
32	  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
33	  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
34	  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
35	  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.
36	
37	- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
38	- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
39	- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).
40	
41	## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session
42	
43	`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.
44	
45	1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
46	2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
47	3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
48	4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
49	5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.
50	
51	If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).
52	
53	## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)
54	
55	- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
56	- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
57	- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.
58	
59	## Conventions
60	
61	- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
62	- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
63	- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
64	- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
65	- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
66	- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
67	- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.
68	
69	## Documentation — keep it current (required)
70	
71	- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
72	- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
73	- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
74	- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.
75	
76	## Commands
77	
78	- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
79	- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
80	- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
81	- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
82	- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
83	- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`
84	
85	## Domains & TLS
86	
87	- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
88	- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
89	- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
90	- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.
91	
92	## Environments
93	
94	- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
95	- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
96	- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Useful for large or highly experimental work in isolation; not part of the normal edit→stage→promote path above. Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
97	- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
98	- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.
99	
100	## Safety rules
101	
102	- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
103	- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
104	- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
105	- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
106	- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
107	- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
108	- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.
109

content.thinking:
Since the real logic lives in components rather than pages, I want to split up exploration across parallel agents by feature area — one covering the whole server management surface (power, reinstall, resize, snapshots, backups, firewall, networking, volumes, etc.) and another covering billing, wallet, and invoices.

Agent B also handles saved cards, auto-renew, checkout correctness for VPS orders, and the referral/affiliate system. Agent C covers domains, DNS, SSL, email, and hosting/sites, while Agent D takes team/org/roles, settings, activity, support, and the remaining misc pages like projects, calendar, and tools. I'll personally verify the nine hypotheses along with job-type cross-checks, href checks, and env flags, then synthesize everything. I'm weighing whether to use the Explore agent type, which is safer since it lacks Edit/Write tools but is meant for locating code rather than auditing it, versus general-purpose agents which have full tool access including edit capabilities — I'm worried about the risk of a subagent accidentally modifying production code, so I'll lean toward strict read-only instructions regardless of which type I use.

Given the audit is on live production, I'm deciding structural safety matters more than raw capability, so I'll go with Explore agents and explicitly instruct them to read full files rather than excerpts to compensate for their typical shallow-read behavior. Before launching them I could gather shared context myself like job type names and env flag conventions, but I'll just let the agents discover that in parallel and handle the hypothesis verification myself afterward.

import { redirect } from "next/navigation";
import type { Role, User } from "@prisma/client";
import { realUser } from "./auth";

/**
 * Role-based access control for the admin ops portal.
 *
 * The admin surface is divided into logical *areas*. Each area maps to the set
 * of staff roles allowed to see and use it. ADMIN implicitly has every area.
 * The admin layout uses this to (a) let any staff role in and (b) hide nav
 * items a role can't reach; each sensitive page additionally gates itself with
 * `requireArea(...)` so a hand-typed URL is refused too.
 */
export type Area =
  | "overview"
  | "analytics"
  | "clients"
  | "support"
  | "fleet"
  | "billing"
  | "accounting"
  | "platform"
  // ---- Narrow areas carved out of "platform"/"support" so a specific tool
  // can be granted to a Role.EMPLOYEE (lib/staff-grants.ts) without opening
  // everything else those buckets also cover. Every OTHER route mapped to
  // "platform"/"support" is untouched — see lib/staff-grants.ts's doc
  // comment for why these six exist as their own areas instead of splitting
  // "platform"/"support" themselves. ADMIN (and, for supportTickets/liveChat,
  // SUPPORT) still reach these exactly as they reach any other area — only
  // EMPLOYEE needs an explicit StaffGrant to use them.
  | "redditTemplates"
  | "companyInbox"
  | "companyMailboxes"
  | "clientsBasic"
  | "supportTickets"
  | "liveChat"
  | "tasks";

/** Which roles may access each area. ADMIN is always allowed (see canAccess). */
export const AREA_ROLES: Record<Area, Role[]> = {
  overview: ["SUPPORT", "BILLING", "ADMIN"],
  analytics: ["ADMIN"],
  clients: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
  support: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
  fleet: ["ADMIN"],
  billing: ["BILLING", "ADMIN"],
  // Real cost/margin data (expenses, net income) — ADMIN only, unlike "billing"
  // (which BILLING-role staff also reach for day-to-day invoice/refund work).
  accounting: ["ADMIN"],
  platform: ["ADMIN"],
  redditTemplates: ["ADMIN"],
  companyInbox: ["ADMIN"],
  companyMailboxes: ["ADMIN"],
  clientsBasic: ["ADMIN"],
  // Identical role list to "support" — legacy SUPPORT-role behavior for
  // tickets/chat is unchanged; only EMPLOYEE needs a StaffGrant for these.
  supportTickets: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
  liveChat: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
  tasks: ["SUPPORT", "BILLING", "ADMIN"],
};

export function canAccess(role: Role, area: Area): boolean {
  return role === "ADMIN" || AREA_ROLES[area].includes(role);
}

/** Any non-customer role that belongs in the ops portal. */
export function isStaff(role: Role): boolean {
  return role === "SUPPORT" || role === "BILLING" || role === "ADMIN";
}

/** Maps admin nav hrefs to their governing area. Unknown routes default to platform (ADMIN-only). */
const HREF_AREA: Record<string, Area> = {
  "/admin": "overview",
  "/admin/analytics": "analytics",
  "/admin/audience": "analytics",
  "/admin/deploy-funnel": "analytics",
  "/admin/partners": "billing",
  "/admin/users": "clients",
  "/admin/support": "supportTickets",
  "/admin/servers": "fleet",
  "/admin/hosting": "fleet",
  "/admin/nxcloud": "fleet",
  "/admin/nodes": "fleet",
  "/admin/ips": "fleet",
  "/admin/provisioning": "fleet",
  "/admin/jobs": "fleet",
  "/admin/monitor": "fleet",
  "/admin/monitoring": "fleet",
  "/admin/backups": "fleet",
  "/admin/abuse": "fleet",
  "/admin/infrastructure": "fleet",
  "/admin/subscriptions": "billing",
  "/admin/billing": "billing",
  "/admin/invoices": "billing",
  "/admin/plans": "billing",
  "/admin/coupons": "billing",
  "/admin/promotions": "platform",
  "/admin/game-plans": "billing",
  "/admin/gift-codes": "billing",
  "/admin/email-plans": "billing",
  "/admin/products": "billing",
  "/admin/affiliate": "billing",
  "/admin/testimonials": "platform",
  "/admin/reviews": "platform",
  "/admin/board": "platform",
  "/admin/feedback": "support",
  "/admin/chat": "liveChat",
  "/admin/mail": "platform",
  "/admin/mailboxes": "companyMailboxes",
  "/admin/inbox": "companyInbox",
  "/admin/clients-basic": "clientsBasic",
  "/admin/tasks": "tasks",
  "/admin/orgs": "clients",
  "/admin/visitors": "analytics",
  "/admin/logs": "platform",
  "/admin/newsletter": "platform",
  "/admin/domains": "platform",
  "/admin/grant": "platform",
  "/admin/audit": "platform",
  "/admin/automation": "platform",
  "/admin/settings": "platform",
  "/admin/staff": "platform",
  "/admin/email-templates": "platform",
  "/admin/games": "platform",
  "/admin/free-minecraft": "fleet",
  "/admin/blog": "platform",
  "/admin/broadcast": "platform",
  "/admin/announcements": "platform",
  // Marketing section.
  "/admin/marketing": "platform",
  "/admin/marketing-hub": "platform",
  "/admin/marketing/studio": "platform",
  "/admin/marketing/assets": "platform",
  "/admin/marketing/calendar": "platform",
  "/admin/reddit": "redditTemplates",
  "/admin/seo": "platform",
  "/admin/seo/settings": "platform",
  "/admin/coldemail": "platform",
  "/admin/coldemail/businesses": "platform",
  "/admin/coldemail/lists": "platform",
  "/admin/coldemail/brands": "platform",
  "/admin/coldemail/campaigns": "platform",
  "/admin/coldemail/suppression": "platform",
  "/admin/coldemail/settings": "platform",
  // Agency (Sitewave) section.
  "/admin/agency": "platform",
  "/admin/agency/pipeline": "platform",
  "/admin/agency/verticals": "platform",
  "/admin/agency/prospects": "platform",
  "/admin/agency/demos": "platform",
  // Ads (Adloop) section.
  "/admin/ads": "platform",
  "/admin/ads/accounts": "platform",
  "/admin/ads/campaigns": "platform",
  "/admin/ads/rules": "platform",
  // Accounting (real revenue/expense tracking).
  "/admin/accounting": "accounting",
  "/admin/accounting/expenses": "accounting",
};

export function areaForHref(href: string): Area {
  return HREF_AREA[href] ?? "platform";
}

export function canAccessHref(role: Role, href: string): boolean {
  return canAccess(role, areaForHref(href));
}

/**
 * Server-side page guard. Redirects to /login if signed out, or back to the
 * overview if the (staff) user's role can't reach this area. Returns the real
 * signed-in user (impersonation is refused elsewhere in the admin layout).
 */
export async function requireArea(area: Area): Promise<User> {
  const user = await realUser();
  if (!user) redirect("/login");
  if (!isStaff(user.role)) redirect("/dashboard");
  if (!canAccess(user.role, area)) redirect("/admin");
  return user;
}

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

- **What's wrong:** The Settings page calls `lib/nx/account.ts:65-66`, which creates `nxk_live_…` keys in the `ApiKey` table.
- **What the API checks:** The only API route, `GET /api/v1/servers`, uses `lib/api-auth.ts`. That code accepts only `nxe_…` tokens and only looks them up in the `ApiToken` table (`:51`, `:57`). Nothing reads `ApiKey`.

  - The one endpoint returns `ip: s.ipAddress` (`route.ts:46`), which is the internal 10.20.x NAT address, and no SSH port.
- **Why it matters:** The public API is advertised but no customer can use it.

**3. Account deletion leaves real services running and destroys billing records (Settings → Delete account)**

  - domains, volumes, NxCloud instances
  - invoices

- **Evidence (DB):** 35 accounts today have hosting, free Minecraft, email or a domain but no active server, so they can delete right now. 6 accounts have already deleted themselves.

  - Deleting orphans cPanel accounts, mailboxes and containers.
  - It wipes invoices that must be kept for tax.
  - Any leftover wallet balance is lost without warning.

**4. Staff are barely told about new tickets (Support)**

  - 1 OPEN ticket has had no reply for 243 hours (since 2026-09-14).

**5. "Active sessions" list is always empty (Settings / Activity)**

**6. An admin impersonating a customer can end up fully logged in as them (Settings)**
- **What's wrong:** `signOutOtherSessions` (`lib/actions-account.ts:54`) and `changePassword` (`:32`) call `createSession(user.id)`, and during impersonation `user` is the customer.
- **Effect:** The admin's own session cookie is replaced by a normal 30-day customer session. The impersonation banner and the `assertNotImpersonating` protection on spending no longer apply, and the customer is signed out everywhere.

- **Fix:** Send the held replies as a digest when the cap resets instead of dropping them.

**8. No security alert emails at all (Settings)**
- **What's wrong:** The `security_change` message type is declared in `lib/prefs.ts`, but nothing ever sends it.
- **Actions that send no email:** password change, 2FA disable, API key creation, new Google link, new sign-in.
- **Missing audit rows:** `changePassword` writes no audit entry, and neither does `createApiKey`.
- **Fix:** Send `security_change` emails from these actions.

**9. Unsupported claims on the dashboard home page**
- **Where:** `components/nx/DashboardView.tsx:59-61`.
- **"Support replies in ~4 min":** measured median first reply is 8.4 min, the mean is 98 min, and one ticket has waited 10 days.
- **"Restore a backup — any point in the last 7 days":** the free tier keeps only 2 daily backups (`lib/backup-tiers.ts`).
- **Rule broken:** CLAUDE.md forbids made-up ETAs.
- **Fix:** Compute the reply time from real data or remove it, and state the customer's actual backup retention.

**10. The Team page promises sharing that doesn't exist (Team)**
- **What the empty state says:** "Organisations let several people share one set of servers and services, each with … their own level of access" (`TeamView.tsx:127`).
- **What membership actually grants:** nothing beyond seeing the roster (`lib/actions-teams.ts:18-25`).
- **Invite bookkeeping bugs:**
  - `acceptInvite` never sets `OrgInvite.acceptedAt`, so accepted invites keep showing as pending and can still be "revoked".
  - The invite link expires after 72 hours, but the pending row says 7 days.
- **Missing:** no way to rename, transfer or delete an organisation.
- **Fix:** Correct the copy now; set `acceptedAt` when an invite is accepted.

**11. Display preferences save but change nothing (Settings)**
- **What's wrong:** Landing page, date format and rows per page are saved to `UserPreference` (`lib/nx/account.ts:27`), but nothing reads them. Only the theme is labelled as "not wired yet".
- **Fix:** Wire them up or hide them.

**12. GDPR data export is incomplete (Settings)**
- **Location:** `app/api/account/export/route.ts`.
- **Included today:** servers, wallet, invoices, domains, tickets, SSH keys, feedback, memberships.
- **Missing:** audit log, hosting, email, free Minecraft, chats and DMs, migrations, notifications, consent records.

**13. Migration is largely unproven in production (Migrate)**
- **Evidence (DB):** 57 runs, all from one customer account, and none since 2026-08-04.
  - 4 finished clean (DONE)
  - 33 finished with issues
  - 20 failed — 16 of those were refused by the source read-only guard
- **Consolidate:** it shows customers the internal env flag name `NXEON_CONSOLIDATE_REMAP` (which is unset) whenever two sources share a path (`lib/actions-migrate.ts`, `startConsolidationMigration`).
- **Partial runs:** the 5-per-10-minutes creation limit can leave a consolidation half-created.
- **Missing guards:** `createMigration` doesn't require the target server to be RUNNING or free of other in-flight jobs.
- **Fix:** Rehearse the full flow on staging, hide the flag name, and add the RUNNING / in-flight checks.

### Low
- **Mobile tab bar shows only "Dashboard":** the mobile list uses `"/deploy"`, `"/servers"`, `"/billing"`, but the nav entries are `/dashboard/...` (`components/nx/Shell.tsx:45`).
- **Feature flags no longer hide nav items:** the layout computes the filtered nav (`FEATURE_HREF` / `visibleNav` / `navWithBadges` in `app/dashboard/layout.tsx`) but never passes it to the new Shell. `/dashboard/claude-code` also doesn't check its flag.
- **No rate limits on tickets and feedback:** `createTicket`, `replyTicket` and `submitFeedback` are unthrottled. Each new ticket opens a Discord channel, and each reply can store up to 6 × 10 MB attachments in Postgres.
- **2FA weak spots:**
  - `disableTotp` accepts the account password alone.
  - No throttling on disable/confirm or on `changePassword`.
  - `regenerateBackupCodes` uses the check that doesn't block code reuse.
- **Ticket creation limits:** no attachments on a new ticket; customers can pick URGENT themselves.
- **Audit log IP never filled:** 0 of 2,105 rows in the last 30 days have an IP, so the Activity IP column is always blank.
- **Google login lands staff in the wrong place:** it sends EMPLOYEE accounts to `/dashboard` instead of `roleHome`. Its link-by-email rule also contradicts the Discord flow, which refuses to merge.
- **Dead-end copy:** the checkout message says to resend verification from "Settings → Email address", which has no resend button. The banner does work.
- **Short lists:** Support loads only 40 tickets with no paging; Activity is capped at 400 rows.
- **Dead code:** `components/customer/SecuritySettings.tsx` and `components/customer/TeamManager.tsx` are imported nowhere.

## Confirmed working (end to end)
- **Tickets:** create → ticket + message + admin bell + Discord mirror → `?ticket=` view.
  - Owner checks on reply, status change, thread and attachments (`actions-support.ts:95-97`, `:227`, `:334`; attachment route `:37`).
  - Attachments are validated and served safely (`nosniff`, CSP sandbox).
  - Staff reply → customer bell + email (156 sent).
- **Close / reopen:** customers can only set OPEN or CLOSED.
- **Team invites:** a real email is sent (2 `team_invite` sent) → the accept page requires the same address → membership created (2 accepted). The owner can't be demoted or removed, and a revoked invite is refused.
- **Password change and "Sign out everywhere else":** both invalidate other sessions. A password reset does not bypass 2FA at the next password login.
- **TOTP 2FA:**
  - Setup, confirm, 10 hashed backup codes, one-time backup-code use, codes can't be reused at login.
  - 8 accounts have it on.
- **Notification preferences are actually applied:** checked centrally in `sendMail` (`lib/mailer.ts:241`); unticking product news also removes the newsletter subscription.
- **Email verification resend:** rate-limited and reports the real result (191 sent, 15 failed).
- **Discord link / unlink:** refuses a Discord account already linked elsewhere.
- **GDPR export download:** own data only, secrets excluded.
- **Feedback:** submit → admin bell; status changes notify the reporter.
- **Projects:** create, and assign from the server page.
- **Nav and links:** all 21 sidebar links resolve, and every internal link in the scoped components points to an existing route.
- **Tools:** all 16 tool pages and 9 API routes exist, with a guard against internal-network lookups.
- **NxLabs:** catalog, game and mod pages link correctly and 404 on bad slugs.
- **Gated pages:**
  - Calendar returns 404 while `feature_calendar` is off.
  - Migrate preview is admin/sandbox only.
- **Migration safety:**
  - The worker won't fake a success if real migration is disabled (it is enabled).
  - No stored source passwords remain (0 rows).

## Account features vs DigitalOcean / Hetzner / Vultr / Hostinger
- **Public API + docs:** half-built. Docs pages exist, but there is one read-only endpoint and the keys the dashboard issues don't work with it. The others offer full create/read/update/delete APIs, OpenAPI specs and CLI/Terraform tooling.
- **API token scopes:** half-built. `ApiToken` supports read/write scopes and expiry but has no UI; the `ApiKey` scope field is decorative.
- **2FA:** TOTP + backup codes present. No WebAuthn/passkeys, bypassable through Google/Discord, and not enforced for staff.
- **Session management:** half-built. Global sign-out works; there is no per-device list or revoke, no new-login alerts, and logout doesn't revoke the session server-side.
- **Audit log:** present per user (Activity, 7/30/90 days). It only shows the viewer's own actions, has no IPs and no export, and there is no org-wide log.
- **Team sub-users with real permissions:** absent (roster only).
- **SSO (SAML/OIDC for customers):** absent. Only Google/Discord social login; Nxeon acts as a sign-in provider for the partner Kodely only.
- **Status page:** present (`/status`, incidents, per-component uptime, also inside Support).
- **Notification channels:** email + in-app only, plus a Discord bridge for support. No SMS, no customer webhooks (the `WebhookEndpoint` table is admin cold-email only), no Slack.
- **Self-service email change:** absent; the page says support must do it.</result>

<result>Nxeon customer portal audit (non-game sections). This was read-only: I changed no files and ran only SELECT queries.

## Findings, most severe first

### High

**1. Google and Discord sign-in skip 2FA (Settings / login)**
- **What's wrong:** The authenticator-code check exists only in the password login, `lib/actions.ts:390`. The Google callback goes straight to `createSession` at `app/api/auth/google/callback/route.ts:183`. The Discord login does the same at `lib/discord-auth.ts:77` and `:118`.
- **Google also links silently by email:** it attaches itself to any existing account with that address (`:117-128`), including staff and admin accounts.
- **Evidence (DB):** 497 of 719 accounts signed up with Google. 56 accounts have Discord linked. 4 accounts have 2FA turned on and also a Google or Discord link, so their 2FA can be bypassed today.
- **Staff:** none of the 4 staff accounts has 2FA, and the `enforce_staff_2fa` setting is off.
- **Why it matters:** A customer who turned on 2FA is not protected when their Google account is compromised — the exact case 2FA exists for.
- **Fix:** When `totpEnabled` is true, the OAuth callbacks should create a pending-2FA state and ask for the code before calling `createSession`.

**2. API keys made in Settings don't work with the API (Settings, API)**
- **What's wrong:** The Settings page calls `lib/nx/account.ts:65-66`, which creates `nxk_live_…` keys in the `ApiKey` table.
- **What the API checks:** The only API route, `GET /api/v1/servers`, uses `lib/api-auth.ts`. That code accepts only `nxe_…` tokens and only looks them up in the `ApiToken` table (`:51`, `:57`). Nothing reads `ApiKey`.
- **The UI that made working tokens is dead:** `components/customer/SecuritySettings.tsx` is not imported anywhere.
- **An invisible live token:** 1 `ApiToken` is still active and never used. The customer cannot see it or revoke it in the current UI.
- **Other problems:**
  - The `/developers` and `/docs` pages advertise scoped tokens and `nxe_live_…` keys.
  - The one endpoint returns `ip: s.ipAddress` (`route.ts:46`), which is the internal 10.20.x NAT address, and no SSH port.
- **Why it matters:** The public API is advertised but no customer can use it.
- **Fix:** Pick one table and one token format. Point Settings at `ApiToken` + `authorizeApiRequest`, and return the address from `connectAddress`.

**3. Account deletion leaves real services running and destroys billing records (Settings → Delete account)**
- **What's wrong:** `lib/actions-gdpr.ts:69` only checks for `Server` rows. Then `db.user.delete` (`:112`) removes, with no teardown job, these linked records:
  - hosting accounts, free Minecraft servers, email subscriptions
  - domains, volumes, NxCloud instances
  - invoices
- **Confirmation is weak:** only typing the email. There is no password or 2FA check, and no impersonation guard.
- **The UI copy is false:** it says "Every service has to be cancelled first" (`SettingsView.tsx:~745`).
- **Evidence (DB):** 35 accounts today have hosting, free Minecraft, email or a domain but no active server, so they can delete right now. 6 accounts have already deleted themselves.
- **Why it matters:**
  - Deleting orphans cPanel accounts, mailboxes and containers.
  - It wipes invoices that must be kept for tax.
  - Any leftover wallet balance is lost without warning.
- **Fix:** Block deletion while any service exists (or queue teardown jobs), keep invoices, require password + 2FA, and add `assertNotImpersonating`.

**4. Staff are barely told about new tickets (Support)**
- **What's wrong:** New tickets and customer replies only create an in-app notification for `role: "ADMIN"` (`lib/reply-core.ts:111`, `:206`). The 2 staff accounts with a `supportTickets` grant get nothing. No email is sent.
- **The admin's notification list is flooded:** 1,942 unread. Most are node alerts ("Node capacity CRITICAL" 532, memory pressure 521). 244 of the unread items are ticket notifications.
- **Evidence (DB):**
  - 1 OPEN ticket has had no reply for 243 hours (since 2026-09-14).
  - 1 ticket in customer-reply state since 09-19.
  - 5 tickets have never received a staff reply.
  - Both waiting tickets were mirrored to Discord.
- **Why it matters:** Paying customers wait days.
- **Fix:** Notify everyone who has support access (in-app and email), add an escalation for unanswered tickets, and move infrastructure alerts out of the same bell.

### Medium

**5. "Active sessions" list is always empty (Settings / Activity)**
- **What's wrong:** Nothing ever writes a `UserSession` row: the table has 0 rows and there is no create call anywhere.
- **Knock-on effects:** "Revoke" on a device (`lib/nx/account.ts:93`) does nothing. The Activity page's sign-in count always says "not recorded".
- **Logout:** it only deletes the cookie (`lib/auth.ts:50`), so a stolen session token stays valid for 30 days.
- **What does work:** "Sign out everywhere else", which bumps a per-account session counter.
- **Fix:** Record a session row in `createSession`, check it in `realUser`, and revoke it on logout.

**6. An admin impersonating a customer can end up fully logged in as them (Settings)**
- **What's wrong:** `signOutOtherSessions` (`lib/actions-account.ts:54`) and `changePassword` (`:32`) call `createSession(user.id)`, and during impersonation `user` is the customer.
- **Effect:** The admin's own session cookie is replaced by a normal 30-day customer session. The impersonation banner and the `assertNotImpersonating` protection on spending no longer apply, and the customer is signed out everywhere.
- **Fix:** Call `assertNotImpersonating()` in both.

**7. Customers silently miss staff reply emails (Support)**
- **What's wrong:** `TICKET_REPLY_DAILY_CAP = 5` (`lib/ticket-reply-email.ts:60`). Once a customer hits it, further reply emails are dropped for good. The catch-up sweep only looks back 30 minutes.
- **Evidence (DB):** 39 "Ticket reply emails paused" flags across 15 tickets (09-01 to 09-23). 5 `ticket_reply` emails FAILED.
- **Fix:** Send the held replies as a digest when the cap resets instead of dropping them.

**8. No security alert emails at all (Settings)**
- **What's wrong:** The `security_change` message type is declared in `lib/prefs.ts`, but nothing ever sends it.
- **Actions that send no email:** password change, 2FA disable, API key creation, new Google link, new sign-in.
- **Missing audit rows:** `changePassword` writes no audit entry, and neither does `createApiKey`.
- **Fix:** Send `security_change` emails from these actions.

**9. Unsupported claims on the dashboard home page**
- **Where:** `components/nx/DashboardView.tsx:59-61`.
- **"Support replies in ~4 min":** measured median first reply is 8.4 min, the mean is 98 min, and one ticket has waited 10 days.
- **"Restore a backup — any point in the last 7 days":** the free tier keeps only 2 daily backups (`lib/backup-tiers.ts`).
- **Rule broken:** CLAUDE.md forbids made-up ETAs.
- **Fix:** Compute the reply time from real data or remove it, and state the customer's actual backup retention.

**10. The Team page promises sharing that doesn't exist (Team)**
- **What the empty state says:** "Organisations let several people share one set of servers and services, each with … their own level of access" (`TeamView.tsx:127`).
- **What membership actually grants:** nothing beyond seeing the roster (`lib/actions-teams.ts:18-25`).
- **Invite bookkeeping bugs:**
  - `acceptInvite` never sets `OrgInvite.acceptedAt`, so accepted invites keep showing as pending and can still be "revoked".
  - The invite link expires after 72 hours, but the pending row says 7 days.
- **Missing:** no way to rename, transfer or delete an organisation.
- **Fix:** Correct the copy now; set `acceptedAt` when an invite is accepted.

**11. Display preferences save but change nothing (Settings)**
- **What's wrong:** Landing page, date format and rows per page are saved to `UserPreference` (`lib/nx/account.ts:27`), but nothing reads them. Only the theme is labelled as "not wired yet".
- **Fix:** Wire them up or hide them.

**12. GDPR data export is incomplete (Settings)**
- **Location:** `app/api/account/export/route.ts`.
- **Included today:** servers, wallet, invoices, domains, tickets, SSH keys, feedback, memberships.
- **Missing:** audit log, hosting, email, free Minecraft, chats and DMs, migrations, notifications, consent records.

**13. Migration is largely unproven in production (Migrate)**
- **Evidence (DB):** 57 runs, all from one customer account, and none since 2026-08-04.
  - 4 finished clean (DONE)
  - 33 finished with issues
  - 20 failed — 16 of those were refused by the source read-only guard
- **Consolidate:** it shows customers the internal env flag name `NXEON_CONSOLIDATE_REMAP` (which is unset) whenever two sources share a path (`lib/actions-migrate.ts`, `startConsolidationMigration`).
- **Partial runs:** the 5-per-10-minutes creation limit can leave a consolidation half-created.
- **Missing guards:** `createMigration` doesn't require the target server to be RUNNING or free of other in-flight jobs.
- **Fix:** Rehearse the full flow on staging, hide the flag name, and add the RUNNING / in-flight checks.

### Low
- **Mobile tab bar shows only "Dashboard":** the mobile list uses `"/deploy"`, `"/servers"`, `"/billing"`, but the nav entries are `/dashboard/...` (`components/nx/Shell.tsx:45`).
- **Feature flags no longer hide nav items:** the layout computes the filtered nav (`FEATURE_HREF` / `visibleNav` / `navWithBadges` in `app/dashboard/layout.tsx`) but never passes it to the new Shell. `/dashboard/claude-code` also doesn't check its flag.
- **No rate limits on tickets and feedback:** `createTicket`, `replyTicket` and `submitFeedback` are unthrottled. Each new ticket opens a Discord channel, and each reply can store up to 6 × 10 MB attachments in Postgres.

<result># Nxeon VPS audit: prioritized findings

I traced each VPS feature from the button through the server action and job to the worker handler. Two of the problems below need fixing first:
- **Critical:** customer VMs behind the shared NAT address can reach each other freely.
- **High:** customer firewall rules are wiped on every reboot and never put back, while the panel still shows them as active.

---

## Findings (most severe first)

### Critical

**1. Networking / tenant isolation: all NAT customer VMs sit on one open private network.**
- **Evidence:**
  - `/etc/network/interfaces`: vmbr1 is a plain Linux bridge.
  - `bridge -d link show`: all 10 vmbr1 ports report `isolated off`.
  - `/proc/sys/net/bridge/bridge-nf-call-iptables` is `0`, so the host firewall never sees VM-to-VM traffic.
  - ebtables FORWARD is empty with policy ACCEPT.
  - `/etc/pve/firewall/` is empty, and no VM config has `firewall=1`.
  - The `nxeon_fw` nft table only filters traffic from vmbr1 to the host and out to the internet, not between VMs.
  - Staging VMs (.50–.99) share this same bridge with production.
- **Why it matters:** any tenant can reach every other tenant's private 10.20.0.x address on any port. That includes databases or admin panels a customer assumed were private. A tenant can also claim another tenant's IP (ARP spoofing) and hijack the inbound SSH/web traffic that NAT forwards to that address. The panel's wording, "private address … only routable inside our network" (`VpsNetworkingPanel.tsx`), makes this look safe when it isn't.
- **Fix:** turn on bridge port isolation for tap ports (or ebtables/PVE firewall with `firewall=1` plus IP filter / anti-spoof per NIC), and move staging to its own bridge. Confirm with two staging VMs first.

### High

**2. Firewall: rules vanish on reboot and are never re-applied, but the panel still lists them as active.**
- **Evidence:**
  - `buildReconcileScript` (`lib/firewall-rules.ts:230-253`) only runs iptables commands inside the guest; nothing saves them to survive a reboot.
  - The only thing that creates `SYNC_FIREWALL` jobs is a rule change in `lib/actions-firewall.ts`. Start, reboot, reinstall, resize, restore, rollback, dedicated-IP power cycles and the crash-recovery sweep never re-sync.
  - `syncFirewall` treats a STOPPED server as "defer", and the job is marked DONE (`worker/firewall.ts`).
  - DB: the only server with rules (8 enabled) last synced at 2026-09-02 15:03:08. It was rebooted at 15:03:53 and hasn't synced since.
  - A failed sync sends the customer no notification.
- **Why it matters:** the UI says rules "take effect within a minute", but the customer's actual protection is most likely gone. This is worst for dedicated-IP servers, where every port faces the internet directly.
- **Fix:** persist the rules in the guest (systemd unit or netfilter-persistent), enqueue `SYNC_FIREWALL` after every power and lifecycle job, show when rules were last applied, and notify on failure. Longer term, enforce at the hypervisor instead.

**3. Error state: any failed power or lifecycle job locks the customer out of the whole server page.**
- **Evidence:**
  - Failures of START, STOP, REBOOT, RESIZE, BACKUP_RESTORE, SNAPSHOT_ROLLBACK and ASSIGN_DEDICATED_IP set the server to ERROR (`worker/index.ts:106-112`, `2520-2522`).
  - The page then returns only the provisioning screen whenever status is ERROR (`page.tsx:340`, `376`). That screen shows "Provisioning failed" and a Contact support button (`components/nx/Provisioning.tsx:175-190`).
  - The retry banner (`ProvisionErrorBanner` / `retryProvision`, `page.tsx:1441`) is dead code for every server type, because the page returns before reaching it.
  - No sweep ever brings a server out of ERROR.
- **Why it matters:** one flaky reboot on an established, working VM takes away Start, the console, restore, cancel and refund. The message tells the customer "the server could not be built", which is wrong for a server that already exists.
- **Fix:** only show the full-page screen for first-time provisioning. For other failures, render the normal panel with an error banner, a Start/retry option, and the real job error.

**4. Billing: VPS customers can't renew manually or turn auto-renew back on (regression since 2026-09-12).**
- **Evidence:**
  - `renewalPanel` (the `RenewalCard` with Renew now and the auto-renew toggle) is defined at `page.tsx:455-482` but never rendered. Commit `013bb73dac` swapped it for the display-only `VpsSubscriptionCard`.
  - `toggleAutoRenew` and `renewNow` have no other caller anywhere in the customer portal.
- **Why it matters:** two messages promise controls that don't exist:
  - The cancel flow says "You can turn auto-renew back on any time before then" (`lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:396`).
  - The billing sweep tells customers "Renew manually before X" and links to the server page (`worker/billing.ts:335`).

  A customer who turns auto-renew off can't undo it, so the server expires, gets suspended and is eventually destroyed. No paid VPS has auto-renew off today. Two game servers do (expiring 2026-10-20), and the game branch doesn't render the card either.
- **Fix:** render `RenewalCard` again (for example in Settings or the subscription card).

**5. Worker: one serial job queue for the whole platform.**
- **Evidence:**
  - The worker claims one job at a time and awaits it inline (`worker/index.ts:3181-3200`). All the periodic sweeps (billing, VM crash recovery, uptime) run in that same loop.
  - A game install can wait up to 45 minutes per attempt (`provision-health.ts:257`), and a backup up to 1 hour (`index.ts:2170`).
  - Live right now: a game PROVISION has been RUNNING since 03:17 with 6 jobs queued behind it.
- **Why it matters:** a VPS customer's Reboot/Start/password reset, and the automatic restart of a crashed VM, wait behind other customers' long jobs. The "within a minute" firewall promise can't be met.
- **Fix:** add a separate fast lane for short VPS jobs (or run per-server jobs concurrently), and move the sweeps onto their own timer.

### Medium

**6. Snapshots: rollback can fail and then lock the server; no limits; failures are silent.**
- **Evidence:**
  - Storage `vmdata` is a ZFS pool (`/etc/pve/storage.cfg`). Proxmox's ZFS backend refuses to roll back to any snapshot that isn't the newest, yet the UI offers Rollback on every row.
  - A failed rollback sets the server to ERROR, which triggers the lockout in finding 3.
  - `createSnapshot` (`lib/actions-server.ts:62`) has no snapshot count or size limit, while the `data` pool is already 80% full and 70% fragmented (`zpool list`).
  - The app accepts names starting with a digit; Proxmox, as far as I know, requires a leading letter.
  - `snapshotOp` (`index.ts:1969-2033`) never notifies the customer on success or failure.
- **Fix:** only offer rollback on the newest snapshot, remove SNAPSHOT_ROLLBACK from the list of failures that set ERROR, cap snapshots per server, validate names the way Proxmox does, and notify on failure. Confirm the ZFS rollback behaviour on staging.

**7. Delete: the More → Delete path skips the refund.**
- `VpsPowerControls.tsx:124-137` calls `serverAction("delete")` (`lib/actions.ts:810-815`), which issues a plain DELETE with no refund. `cancelService` (`lifecycle.ts:405-471`) is the only path that refunds unused time.
- The dialog only says "Any remaining term is handled by the cancellation flow…" (line 133). The same path also destroys attached volumes without warning in the dialog.
- **Fix:** route Delete through `cancelService("immediate")`, or remove it from the menu.

**8. Power: Stop pulls the plug, and a hung guest can't be recovered cleanly.**
- STOP maps to Proxmox `status/stop` (`index.ts:1404`), which is an immediate power-off. There is no graceful shutdown and no reset.
- On a hung guest, Reboot (which needs the guest to cooperate) fails, and that feeds finding 3.
- **Fix:** add Shutdown (graceful) and Reset (hard) as separate actions, and make Stop graceful with a hard-stop fallback.

**9. Dedicated IPv4: advertised as included, but new servers silently get NAT when the pool runs out.**
- `provision()` only logs "This customer paid for an IP they did not receive" to the console and carries on with NAT (`index.ts:779-793`).
- Marketing claims a dedicated IPv4 comes with the VPS (`app/llms.txt/route.ts:73`, `app/(marketing)/gaming-vps/page.tsx:10`).
- DB: 11 of 17 VPS are on NAT, and the pool has 1 free customer IP left.
- **Fix:** alert an admin and tell the customer when this happens, or fix the marketing copy.

**10. Volumes: the advice for keeping volume data is impossible to follow.**
- Reinstall and restore refuse while a volume is assigned. The reinstall error tells the customer to "attach the volume to a different server first" (`lifecycle.ts:162-168`).
- `attachVolume` refuses exactly that (`actions-volumes.ts:148-151`).
- So a customer with volume data can never reinstall or restore without destroying the volume.
- **Fix:** support moving a volume between the customer's own servers on the same node, or correct the message.

**11. Reinstall keeps the old root password.**
- `index.ts:757` reuses the stored password whenever the server already has a VM ID, which is always true on reinstall.
- **Fix:** generate a new password on REINSTALL.

**12. Firewall script is fragile.**
- No `set -e`, so the exit code is whatever the last line returned; a partial apply is reported as success.
- It assumes `iptables` exists in the guest, but cloud-init only installs qemu-guest-agent. It has only been used on Ubuntu 24.04.
- It connects over SSH with the stored root password, so a customer who changes their password or disables password login breaks it.

### Low

13. **Backups wording:**
    - `page.tsx:743` calls backup storage "separate, redundant". Customer archives actually live on the `tank` pool, which is a single disk (`sda`). The platform's nightly off-site copy is separate from what customers can restore.
    - `page.tsx:759` says "restores are handled by support", yet self-service restore exists.
    - Automatic backups are off by default; only 7 of 37 servers have them on.
14. **Reverse DNS (rDNS) is admin-only** (`lib/actions-ovh.ts:30`). `setDedicatedReverse` quietly does nothing if the provider isn't configured (`lib/dedicated-ip.ts:421-431`), and the PTR record isn't reset when an IP goes back to the pool.
15. **The crash-recovery sweep restarts servers customers shut down themselves.** It restarts any VM marked RUNNING in the DB that is found powered off, including after an in-guest `poweroff`, within about 5 minutes (`worker/vm-recovery.ts:35,62-69`).
16. **A server being deleted shows "Building your server"**, because DELETING counts as transitional (`page.tsx:340` / `Provisioning.tsx:242`).
17. **Port forwards:**
    - `addPortForward` doesn't reject a duplicate guest port, although a comment in `NetworkingControls.tsx:14-19` says it does.
    - The "Allow HTTP (80)" preset actually maps a random public port between 20000 and 29999.
    - A NAT VPS can't serve on ports 80/443 at all.
18. **Overview "Create backup" button** is only a link to the Backups tab (`VpsOverviewPanel.tsx:442`).
19. **Failed-resize refund:** if a resize fails after the plan was already switched, the customer is refunded without the plan being switched back (`index.ts:1846` vs `2432-2439`).
20. **SSH keys** are only injected at provision/reinstall; deleting a key from the account doesn't remove it from existing servers. The UI copy is honest about this.
21. **Suspended banner** links to "Open a ticket" instead of the billing page, which is where an unpaid suspension is actually settled.
22. **NxCloud** is switched off (`nxcloud_ordering_enabled=false`, 0 instances). If it's enabled later, its backing server is still reachable at `/dashboard/servers/[id]` with full reinstall/delete controls, and `terminateNxcloud` gives no refund and doesn't check for a running job.

---

## Working end to end

- **Power start/stop/reboot:** `serverAction` (`lib/actions.ts:762`) → `powerAction` (`worker/index.ts:1394`). All DONE in the last 30 days.
- **Reinstall, same OS or a new OS:** `reinstallToOs` (`lifecycle.ts:121`) → `reinstall()` (`index.ts:1569`), with a guard for attached volumes. 4 DONE.
- **Resize up with proration:** `resizeServer` → `applyResize` (`lib/resize.ts:158`) → `resize()` (`index.ts:1790`), refund on failure (`index.ts:2414`). Only exercised once on a VPS (July).
- **Disk expand:** `expandServerDisk` → `worker/disk-expand.ts` (grows the filesystem online, refunds if it fails). 5 DONE.
- **Dedicated IP add-on:** `purchaseDedicatedIp` → `assignDedicatedIp` (`index.ts:1896`) plus refund on failure. Checks the pool before charging. 3 DONE.
- **Manual backups:** `createBackup` → `backupCreate` (`index.ts:2119`), which confirms the archive exists and notifies on failure. 139 DONE, 0 FAILED.
- **Scheduled backups and Plus tier:** `setBackupSchedule` → `worker/backup-schedule.ts`; `upgradeServerBackupTier` also turns automatic backups on. No stale schedules.
- **Restore:** `requestRestore` (`actions-server-ops.ts:128`) → `worker/restore.ts`. The false "net0 mismatch" failure was fixed on 2026-09-12; two restores succeeded on 2026-09-23 (on game servers, which use the same code).
- **Backup download:** `/api/servers/[id]/backups/download`, checks ownership and that the archive belongs to this server.
- **Root password reset:** `resetRootPassword` → `passwordReset` (`index.ts:2035`). 8 DONE.
- **Port forwards:** `addPortForward` → `syncPortForwards` (`worker/network.ts`), which rebuilds and verifies the NAT rules per node.
- **VNC console:** `/api/console/[serverId]` issues an encrypted one-time ticket to the console relay; the noVNC files are present.
- **Metrics:** `/api/metrics` for CPU/RAM/network history and `/api/servers/[id]/disk` for disk. 15 of 17 VPS have disk readings from the last 24 hours. Bandwidth is metered by `worker/monitor.ts`.
- **Cancel:** `cancelService` supports cancel-at-period-end and immediate termination with a protected wallet refund.
- **Volumes:** order/attach/detach/delete → `worker/volumes.ts` (formats and mounts safely). Exercised in production.
- **Rename and project assignment:** both check ownership.

Every server action I read checks ownership (owner or admin) before doing anything.

## Compared with DigitalOcean, Hetzner Cloud and Vultr

| Feature | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Rescue mode | Absent | No code anywhere |
| ISO mount / custom ISO | Absent | No code anywhere |
| Floating IPs | Absent | A dedicated IP is tied to one server; it can't be moved or released |
| Private networking / VPC | Absent, and the shared NAT network is unisolated | Finding 1 |
| Cloud firewall / firewall groups | Half-built | Rules per server, applied inside the guest, lost on reboot (finding 2) |
| Monitoring alerts for customers | Absent for VPS | `ResourceLimitAlert` is only used in the game panel |
| Scheduled backups with restore | Present | Off by default; restore, download and paid retention tier work |
| Bandwidth accounting | Half-built | Metered and displayed; no overage billing or throttling |
| Resize down | Absent in the UI | `resizeServerDown` exists but nothing calls it; the UI points to support |
| Serial console | Absent | VNC only, plus a password-based web SSH terminal |
| Reverse DNS | Half-built | Admin-only (finding 14) |
| IPv6 | Absent | 0 servers have an IPv6 address |
| Snapshots | Present with caveats | Finding 6 |
| API for managing servers | Absent | `/api/v1/servers` is read-only listing |
| Graceful shutdown vs. reset | Absent | Stop is a hard power-off only |
| SSH keys | Half-built | Applied at deploy/reinstall only, no per-server management |

**Process notes:**

- **High:** customer firewall rules are wiped on every reboot and never put back, while the panel still shows them as active.

  - `bridge -d link show`: all 10 vmbr1 ports report `isolated off`.

  - ebtables FORWARD is empty with policy ACCEPT.
  - `/etc/pve/firewall/` is empty, and no VM config has `firewall=1`.
  - The `nxeon_fw` nft table only filters traffic from vmbr1 to the host and out to the internet, not between VMs.
  - Staging VMs (.50–.99) share this same bridge with production.
- **Why it matters:** any tenant can reach every other tenant's private 10.20.0.x address on any port. That includes databases or admin panels a customer assumed were private. A tenant can also claim another tenant's IP (ARP spoofing) and hijack the inbound SSH/web traffic that NAT forwards to that address. The panel's wording, "private address … only routable inside our network" (`VpsNetworkingPanel.tsx`), makes this look safe when it isn't.
- **Fix:** turn on bridge port isolation for tap ports (or ebtables/PVE firewall with `firewall=1` plus IP filter / anti-spoof per NIC), and move staging to its own bridge. Confirm with two staging VMs first.

### High

**2. Firewall: rules vanish on reboot and are never re-applied, but the panel still lists them as active.**
- **Evidence:**
  - `buildReconcileScript` (`lib/firewall-rules.ts:230-253`) only runs iptables commands inside the guest; nothing saves them to survive a reboot.
  - The only thing that creates `SYNC_FIREWALL` jobs is a rule change in `lib/actions-firewall.ts`. Start, reboot, reinstall, resize, restore, rollback, dedicated-IP power cycles and the crash-recovery sweep never re-sync.
  - `syncFirewall` treats a STOPPED server as "defer", and the job is marked DONE (`worker/firewall.ts`).
  - DB: the only server with rules (8 enabled) last synced at 2026-09-02 15:03:08. It was rebooted at 15:03:53 and hasn't synced since.
  - A failed sync sends the customer no notification.
- **Why it matters:** the UI says rules "take effect within a minute", but the customer's actual protection is most likely gone. This is worst for dedicated-IP servers, where every port faces the internet directly.
- **Fix:** persist the rules in the guest (systemd unit or netfilter-persistent), enqueue `SYNC_FIREWALL` after every power and lifecycle job, show when rules were last applied, and notify on failure. Longer term, enforce at the hypervisor instead.

**3. Error state: any failed power or lifecycle job locks the customer out of the whole server page.**
- **Evidence:**
  - Failures of START, STOP, REBOOT, RESIZE, BACKUP_RESTORE, SNAPSHOT_ROLLBACK and ASSIGN_DEDICATED_IP set the server to ERROR (`worker/index.ts:106-112`, `2520-2522`).

  - The retry banner (`ProvisionErrorBanner` / `retryProvision`, `page.tsx:1441`) is dead code for every server type, because the page returns before reaching it.
  - No sweep ever brings a server out of ERROR.
- **Why it matters:** one flaky reboot on an established, working VM takes away Start, the console, restore, cancel and refund. The message tells the customer "the server could not be built", which is wrong for a server that already exists.
- **Fix:** only show the full-page screen for first-time provisioning. For other failures, render the normal panel with an error banner, a Start/retry option, and the real job error.

**4. Billing: VPS customers can't renew manually or turn auto-renew back on (regression since 2026-09-12).**
- **Evidence:**
  - `renewalPanel` (the `RenewalCard` with Renew now and the auto-renew toggle) is defined at `page.tsx:455-482` but never rendered. Commit `013bb73dac` swapped it for the display-only `VpsSubscriptionCard`.
  - `toggleAutoRenew` and `renewNow` have no other caller anywhere in the customer portal.
- **Why it matters:** two messages promise controls that don't exist:
  - The cancel flow says "You can turn auto-renew back on any time before then" (`lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:396`).
  - The billing sweep tells customers "Renew manually before X" and links to the server page (`worker/billing.ts:335`).

  A customer who turns auto-renew off can't undo it, so the server expires, gets suspended and is eventually destroyed. No paid VPS has auto-renew off today. Two game servers do (expiring 2026-10-20), and the game branch doesn't render the card either.
- **Fix:** render `RenewalCard` again (for example in Settings or the subscription card).

**5. Worker: one serial job queue for the whole platform.**
- **Evidence:**
  - The worker claims one job at a time and awaits it inline (`worker/index.ts:3181-3200`). All the periodic sweeps (billing, VM crash recovery, uptime) run in that same loop.
  - A game install can wait up to 45 minutes per attempt (`provision-health.ts:257`), and a backup up to 1 hour (`index.ts:2170`).
  - Live right now: a game PROVISION has been RUNNING since 03:17 with 6 jobs queued behind it.
- **Why it matters:** a VPS customer's Reboot/Start/password reset, and the automatic restart of a crashed VM, wait behind other customers' long jobs. The "within a minute" firewall promise can't be met.
- **Fix:** add a separate fast lane for short VPS jobs (or run per-server jobs concurrently), and move the sweeps onto their own timer.

**6. Snapshots: rollback can fail and then lock the server; no limits; failures are silent.**
- **Evidence:**
  - Storage `vmdata` is a ZFS pool (`/etc/pve/storage.cfg`). Proxmox's ZFS backend refuses to roll back to any snapshot that isn't the newest, yet the UI offers Rollback on every row.
  - A failed rollback sets the server to ERROR, which triggers the lockout in finding 3.
  - `createSnapshot` (`lib/actions-server.ts:62`) has no snapshot count or size limit, while the `data` pool is already 80% full and 70% fragmented (`zpool list`).
  - The app accepts names starting with a digit; Proxmox, as far as I know, requires a leading letter.
  - `snapshotOp` (`index.ts:1969-2033`) never notifies the customer on success or failure.

- **Manual backups:** `createBackup` → `backupCreate` (`index.ts:2119`), which confirms the archive exists and notifies on failure. 139 DONE, 0 FAILED.

## Prioritized findings

### Critical

**1. Email / Domains: mail DNS is never published for Nxeon-registered domains, but the UI says it is.**
- **What's wrong:** Both the free Domain Inbox and paid Business Email on an in-account domain are created `external:false, verified:true`. No code ever writes MX, SPF, DKIM or DMARC records:
  - `/opt/nxeon/lib/domain-inbox-email.ts:101-118`
  - `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:348-457`
  - `addRecord` is only ever called from the manual DNS UI (`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains-dns.ts`, `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains.ts`).
- **The UI claims otherwise:** "its mail DNS is managed for you — mailboxes go live automatically" (`/opt/nxeon/components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx:883-895`).
- **The customer has no in-product way to fix it:**
  - The DKIM value is only shown by `EmailDnsSetup`, which renders for external domains only.
  - `autoCreateEmailDns` and `verifyEmailDomain` refuse non-external subscriptions (`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:1181`, `:671`).
  - The DNS Quick setup has no Nxeon-mail preset. Its generic SPF preset is `v=spf1 ~all`, which authorises nobody (`/opt/nxeon/components/customer/DnsQuickSetup.tsx:206`).
- **Evidence (live DNS):** the only Free Domain Inbox has an ACTIVE mailbox, but its MX does not point at Nxeon mail and there is no SPF or DKIM record.
- **Why it matters:** "Free business email with every domain" is a headline promise, and paid email on Nxeon domains silently receives nothing.
- **Fix:** on subscription/mailbox creation for in-account domains, push MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC through `addDnsRecordsBulk`. Also show the record panel for all subscriptions, not just external ones.

**2. Email (security): anyone can make the shared Mailcow treat any domain as local, without proving ownership.**
- **What's wrong:** `getEmailDnsRecords` calls `mcCreateDomain` for unverified external subscriptions (`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:592-597`). `orderEmailHosting` accepts any syntactically valid domain with no denylist. Hosting orders also accept any domain with no ownership check (`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-hosting.ts:161-187`) and bundle a free email subscription.
- **Why it matters:** platform SMTP (`Setting smtp_host` = internal 10.20.0.10, i.e. Mailcow) and every customer mailbox relay through that Mailcow. If someone claims a major mailbox provider's domain, mail to that domain from every Nxeon mailbox — and from the platform itself if it relays through Mailcow — would be handled locally and bounce. That includes password resets and invoices. Cost to the attacker could be as low as $0 (first-month-free hosting plus bundled email). I found no sign it has been exploited.
- **Fix:** never call `mcCreateDomain` before verification (fetch DKIM after verifying), and add a denylist of public mailbox providers.

### High

**3. Domains: search shows one registrar's availability and price, but checkout charges another registrar's price.**
- Namecheap is enabled (`Setting registrar_namecheap_enabled=true`) and all four of its env vars are set, so search merges the cheapest "available" result across both registrars (`/opt/nxeon/lib/tools/domain-availability.ts:40-47`).
- `purchaseDomain` re-quotes from name.com only (`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains.ts:497`), with no `expectedCents` comparison (the transfer flow does have one).
- Nothing ever registers through Namecheap: `registrarById` is unused.
- **Evidence:** 167 "availability disagreement" log lines in 30 days (72 `.au`, 49 `.com`).
- **Why it matters:** customers are either charged a price they weren't shown, or hit "Domain is not available" on a domain the UI just called available.
- **Fix:** restrict search to registrars that can actually fulfil the order, and pass the displayed price for a server-side equality check.

**4. Domains: auto-renew is wallet-only and alerts are in-app only, so domains can lapse.**
- Auto-renew never charges the saved card (`/opt/nxeon/worker/billing.ts:1952-1971`). The wizard's `useWallet` defaults off, so card buyers typically have a $0 wallet.
- The failure alert is an in-app notification, not an email.
- `domainExpiringWarningSweep` only covers `autoRenew=false` domains (`/opt/nxeon/worker/billing.ts:2090-2096`).
- The renewal window is 7 days, and nothing ever moves a domain to EXPIRED.
- **Why it matters:** a customer who bought by card can lose the domain without ever receiving an email.
- **Fix:** attempt a card charge like server renewals do, send email, and widen the window to around 30 days.

Domains: the WHOIS privacy toggle only flips a DB column.** `setWhoisPrivacy` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts:94-113`) never calls the registrar, yet the switch and the Overview "Privacy protection" tile change state. **Fix:** call name.com `:enableWhoisPrivacy` / `:disableWhoisPrivacy`, or make the control read-only.

**6. Domains: nameservers can't be reverted and are never read back from the registrar.**

- **Fix:** read live nameservers from `domainInfo`, add "restore default nameservers", and warn on the DNS tab when delegated elsewhere.
